name: entire-trail-review-loop
description: Bring an Entire Graph trail current, ensure every runner has a fresh evaluation, and loop on findings until the final head has zero open findings. Use for “check all runners,” “update the trail,” or “address all findings.”
argument-hint: "<trail-number>"
disable-model-invocation: true
allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Bash
---

# Entire trail review loop

## When to use

Use in a compatible `entire-graph` checkout when a user asks to review a trail, make its branch current with `main`, ensure runner coverage, resolve findings, or verify mergeability. Do not use it to bypass a required human approval or to claim a time-specific trail is ready without fresh evidence.

## Inputs / context

1. Confirm trail number `$0`, checkout, base branch, and configured `.entire/runners/`.
2. Read `entire agent-help` for every CLI command before relying on flags.
3. Capture current head, ahead/behind against `origin/main`, finding state, runner state, and mergeability.

## Procedure

1. Check out the target trail and synchronize it with `origin/main` when behind. Resolve merge conflicts and validate the resulting head before pushing.
2. Inspect every configured runner. Push an explicitly empty commit when push-only runners need a new evaluation. For runners that support manual starts, use `entire api --to cell -X POST '/api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/trails/$0/runs/<runner-id>'`.
3. Wait for all configured runners to evaluate the current head. Query findings with `entire trail finding $0 --freshness any --status any --json`.
4. For each open finding, reproduce it with a focused regression test, make the smallest sound fix, run focused plus relevant broader validation, push, and repeat runner/finding checks on the new head.
5. Verify the final head: all runners have evaluated/passed as applicable, `--status open` reports `Open: 0`, branch ahead/behind is explicit, technical CI is fresh, and mergeability is queried separately.
6. If a session/checkpoint is in scope, verify remote checkpoint artifacts in addition to local attachment output.

## Efficiency plan

- Read runner definitions once and keep a runner-state table while revisions change.
- Query only the target trail and its final head; do not treat an earlier clean dashboard as final.
- Use focused regressions to guide each fix, then run the relevant full guard suite once the fix is stable.
- Stop when final-head evidence is complete; do not wait indefinitely for a human approval gate outside agent control.

## Pitfalls and fixes

- `mise run check` reports that `mise.toml` is untrusted -> use `MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS="$PWD" mise run check` or deliberately trust the repo before diagnosing code.
- `JSONDecodeError: Extra data` from a raw trail-detail API call -> use `/api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/trails/$0`, not the generic `/api/v1/trails/...` path.
- CI is green but Entire says not mergeable -> inspect `approvalGatePassed`; report missing human approval as a separate non-code blocker.
- A fresh review discovers a finding after prior zero findings -> continue the loop; the prior dashboard covered an older revision.

## Verification checklist

- Every configured runner was inspected and is fresh for the final head.
- `entire trail finding $0 --freshness any --status open --json` shows `Open: 0`.
- Focused regression tests and applicable broader validation passed on the final code.
- Ahead/behind, CI/check status, GitHub mergeability, and Entire approval gate are each reported distinctly.
- Any remaining human approval is explicitly identified rather than described as a code or CI failure.
"}}

  "body": "Problem:\nSearch ranking degrades when prose queries use different word forms than code identifiers. Specifically:\n\"logs a user in\" (split across tokens) failed to find the login identifier because the verb was separated from its particle.\n\"authentication\" (full spelling) matched none of the auth-named functions, returning wrong results.\nSubstring matching caused false positives: \"login\" substring appeared in unrelated identifiers like runLogging, leading to incorrect ranking.\n\"write the log in json format\" incorrectly matched login functions instead of logging ones.\nSolution:\nFour targeted fixes to query term extraction and name-based ranking:\nTokenized name matching: Replaced raw substring search with token-boundary matching in searchNameTokenMatchesTerm, so \"log\" only matches the log token, not a substring of login. Restores the ability to distinguish login from logging identifiers.\nSeparable phrasal verb recovery: Added searchCompoundJoins to detect phrasal verbs split by their objects in prose—\"logs a user in\" now recovers the joined term login by scanning for patterns up to 3 tokens apart. Determiner and object-head checks prevent false positives (\"write the log in JSON\" stays excluded).\nAbbreviation table and alias expansion: Introduced searchTermAbbreviations mapping 48 common prose spellings to code abbreviations (authentication→auth, configuration→config, etc.). entire api — Make an authenticated request to an Entire API and print the response
Make an authenticated HTTP request to an Entire API and print the JSON response.

These endpoints are internal and can change shape without notice; where a
purpose-built command exists, its output is the stable interface.

The CLI attaches the right bearer token and dials the right host for the
chosen backend, so you don't have to plumb auth yourself:

  --to core   the control plane (default): orgs, repos, mirrors, clusters, /me
  --to cell   your home entire-api cell: /me/* activity, repo aggregates

Use --jurisdiction <slug> (e.g. us, eu) to reach a specific jurisdiction's
entire-api cell instead of your home one; it implies --to cell.

<path> is the full path on that host, e.g. /api/v1/clusters. These
placeholders are filled from the current repo's origin remote:
  {owner} {repo}   the GitHub owner / repo
  {repo_id}        the repo's Entire ULID (from its mirror) — cells key on this

The method is GET unless a field/body is given (then POST); override with -X.

When to use this:
LAST RESORT. Right in two cases: you are developing against Entire's own
APIs and want a raw response, or no first-class command covers your need.
Otherwise prefer the command built for the job (checkpoint, session, trail,
status, repo, …) — its output is stable, raw endpoints are not. If you are
reaching for this during ordinary work in a repo with Entire enabled, run
`entire agent-help` first; there is probably a command for it. When you do
need it, use this rather than hand-rolling curl — it attaches the right
bearer and dials the right host for you.

Examples:
entire api /api/v1/clusters
  entire api --to cell /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --jurisdiction eu /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --to cell "/api/v1/me/recap?repo={repo_id}"
  entire api -X POST /api/v1/projects -f name=demo

Current repo: gh/entireio/entire-graph  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
  -F, --field stringArray       add a typed parameter in key=value format; true/false/null/numbers are converted (repeatable)
  -H, --header stringArray      add a request header in key:value format (repeatable)
  -i, --include                 print the response status line and headers too
      --input string            file with the request body ("-" for stdin)
  -j, --jurisdiction string     target a specific jurisdiction's cell (e.g. us, eu) instead of your home cell; implies --to cell
  -X, --method string           HTTP method (default GET, or POST when a field/body is given)
  -f, --raw-field stringArray   add a string parameter in key=value format (repeatable)
      --to string               which backend to call: core or cell (default "core")

Inherited flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

1. **Plural queries miss abbreviation retrieval.** `configuration` finds `loadConfig` and `applyConfigDefaults`; `configurations` finds neither in the supplied corpus. Alias expansion uses the terms captured before singularization. Expand aliases from normalized variants too.

2. **Logging phrases incorrectly generate `login`.** Both “log the error in json” and “log a message in json format” add `login`, raising authentication functions above relevant logging results. The object-head check does not distinguish a login particle from a formatting preposition.

::code-comment{title="[P2] Expand abbreviations from morphological variants" body="The abbreviation loop uses originalTerms, captured before morphological expansion. Consequently configurations produces configuration but never config or cfg, and both config functions disappear from the supplied retrieval corpus. Expand aliases from normalized variants as well." file="/tmp/entire-graph-review-181/internal/sem/search.go" start=5127 end=5129 priority=2}
::code-comment{title="[P2] Avoid interpreting logging formats as login" body="The separated-particle scan converts log the error in json and log a message in json format into login queries. Both reproduce, and the latter raises persistLogin above relevant logging results in the supplied corpus. Add a guard and regression coverage for formatting prepositions." file="/tmp/entire-graph-review-181/internal/sem/search.go" start=4983 end=4987 priority=2}

Existing semantic suite passed; added reproductions fail as described. CI: **25 passed**. Runners: **6 passed, semantic-diff not run**. Branch: **4 ahead, 0 behind**, conflict-free; human approval remains outstanding. No production changes made.

[tools]
go = { version = "1.27" }

[tasks.fmt]
description = "Run gofmt"
run = "gofmt -s -w ."

# Test fixtures create real Git repositories and commit to them. Without the env
# below they inherit the developer's global and system Git config, and anything
# there that makes `git commit` wait -- commit.gpgsign against a hardware key is
# the one that bites -- is paid once per fixture commit. Neutering both files
# took the dependents tests from 27s to 0.3s locally. CI never noticed: its
# runners have no user config to inherit.
[tasks.test]
description = "Run tests"
env = { GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL = "/dev/null", GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM = "/dev/null" }
run = "go test -timeout 30m ./..."

[tasks.vet]
description = "Run go vet"
run = "go vet ./..."

[tasks."test:ci"]
description = "Run tests with race detection"
env = { GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL = "/dev/null", GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM = "/dev/null" }
run = "go test -race -timeout 30m ./..."

[tasks."test:statusline"]
description = "Test the Claude Code status line script"
depends = ["build"]
run = "sh scripts/entire-graph-statusline_test.sh"

[tasks.build]
description = "Build the plugin binary"
run = "go build -o entire-graph ./cmd/entire-graph"

[tasks.install]
description = "Build and install the plugin into the local Entire CLI"
run = "scripts/install-local.sh"

[tasks.release]
description = "Build checksum-backed release archives under dist/"
run = "scripts/release.sh"

[tasks.check]
description = "Run formatting, vet, tests, and build"
depends = ["fmt", "vet", "test:ci", "test:statusline", "build"]

run = "go vet ./..."

[tasks."test:ci"]
description = "Run tests with race detection"
env = { GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL = "/dev/null", GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM = "/dev/null" }
run = "go test -race -timeout 30m ./..."

[tasks."test:statusline"]
description = "Test the Claude Code status line script"
depends = ["build"]
run = "sh scripts/entire-graph-statusline_test.sh"

[tasks.build]
description = "Build the plugin binary"
run = "go build -o entire-graph ./cmd/entire-graph"

[tasks.install]
description = "Build and install the plugin into the local Entire CLI"
run = "scripts/install-local.sh"

[tasks.release]
description = "Build checksum-backed release archives under dist/"
run = "scripts/release.sh"

[tasks.check]
description = "Run formatting, vet, tests, and build"
depends = ["fmt", "vet", "test:ci", "test:statusline", "build"]
"}

Adopt an active session from another worktree into the current repository.

This is useful when an agent starts in one repository or worktree, then moves
and makes changes in another. Adoption moves the live session state into the
current repo and seeds it with the current repo's uncommitted file changes so
the next commit can be linked normally.

When the source and target share a Git session store, adoption moves the same
session state file to the current worktree and requires --force or --yes.

entire trail finding — Manage a trail's agent findings
Manage a trail's agent-native findings.

Running 'entire trail finding' shows the finding dashboard for the current
branch's trail. Pass a trail selector (number, id, or branch) to inspect another
trail in the same repo. Use 'entire trail list --status any' when you need to
discover a trail selector first.

Current repo: gh/entireio/entire-graph  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
      --branch string       Resolve the trail for this branch instead of the current branch; cannot be combined with a trail selector
      --freshness string    Filter code-version freshness: current,stale,any (default "current")
      --include-dismissed   Include dismissed findings
      --json                Output as JSON
  -n, --limit int           Maximum number of findings to show (default 100)
      --offset int          Pagination offset
      --severity string     Filter by comma-separated severity value(s): high,medium,low
      --status string       Filter by lifecycle status(es): open,resolved,dismissed; use 'any' for all (default "open")
      --trail string        Trail selector (number, id, or branch); defaults to the current branch's trail

Inherited flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
      --repo string    Target repository as forge/owner/repo (e.g. gh/acme/app) or a clone URL; defaults to the origin remote

Subcommands: add · apply · dismiss · list · reopen · resolve · show · update
             task-driven
